title: Glen Lough Walking Route

images.title: Glenieraragh Townland by Kenneth Allen, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Glenieraragh Townland. View of Glen Lough. The lough measures about 3 km (2 mi) long and 0.5 km (0.3 mi) wide and lies just north of Lough Beagh and Glenveagh National Park. The Derryveagh Mountains begin on the lake's western side and the Glendowan Mountains begin on the lake's southern end. Glen Lough is fed mainly by the Owencarrow River entering at its southern end. The lake drains northwards into the Lackagh River, which in turn enters Sheephaven Bay. The Owencarrow connects the lake with its southern neighbour, Lough Beagh.

images.caption: Lane, Glenieraugh

description: This walk visits Glen Lough in north County Donegal. The lake is located just to the east of the village of Creeslough.On the eastern side of the lake there's quiet lanes where you can enjoy a peaceful walk or cycle. Here you can enjoy some excellent views over the water to the Derryveagh Mountains and the Glendowan Mountains.To continue your walking in the area try theMuckish Railway Walk.
